age.evidence: adult male C57BL/6J mice (10-18 weeks old; Jackson Laboratory, United States)

sex.evidence: All experiments were conducted in adult male C57BL/6J mice

dosing.evidence: treated with single intraperitoneal injection of saline or 25 or 50 µg/kg LSD (25 or 50 µg/kg body weight, i.p.) once before the onset of the dark cycle

day_night_flipped.evidence: Mice were housed singly and habituated to reverse light-dark cycle for at least a week

assays.assay_description: Singly-housed mice were exposed to two bottles (water and 20% ethanol) for 24 h at the start of the dark phase, 5 days/week for 4 weeks to develop preference. After LSD/saline injection, consumption was measured daily for up to 46 days. Outcomes: ethanol consumption (g/kg/day), ethanol preference, total fluid intake.

application_type.evidence: single intraperitoneal injection of saline or 25 or 50 µg/kg LSD

setup_habituation.evidence: Mice were housed singly and habituated to reverse light-dark cycle for at least a week. The mice were then exposed to ethanol to develop preference... for 4 weeks

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were freely moving in their home cage during drinking

food_restriction.evidence: Mice were given unlimited access to standard mouse chow and water throughout the entire study

water_restriction.evidence: Mice were given unlimited access to standard mouse chow and water throughout the entire study

time_to_assay.evidence: Water bottles were replaced with bottles containing water and ethanol after 10 min of treatment

sample_size.evidence: Data are presented as mean ± SEM (n = 8-10 per group)

outcomes.summary: A single 50 µg/kg i.p. dose of LSD reduced ethanol consumption (~17.9%) and ethanol preference compared to saline controls, with the effect sustained for 46 days. 25 µg/kg LSD had no significant effect. Total fluid intake did not differ between groups.
outcomes.evidence: In mice treated with 50 µg/kg LSD ethanol consumption was reduced relative to controls (p = 0.0035), as was ethanol preference (p = 0.0024)... No significant effects on ethanol consumption or preference were observed in mice treated with 25 µg/kg LSD

B1_num_measures.evidence: ethanol consumption, ethanol preference, and total fluid intake measured

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Data reported as daily 24-h totals across days; no within-session time-course analysis reported

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: no analysis of behavioural sequences reported

B4_ethological.evidence: drinking preference is not scored as an ethological behaviour

B5_social.evidence: Mice were housed singly and tested alone

B6_cognitive.evidence: two-bottle choice does not require learning/memory in the rubric sense

E1_environment_type.evidence: Mice were housed singly... offered water and 20% ethanol in the home cage

E2_shelter.evidence: no shelter described in the home cage

E8_food_water.evidence: Mice were given unlimited access to standard mouse chow and water throughout the entire study

D1_continuity.evidence: Amounts of ethanol and water consumption were measured every 24 h for 5 days/week

D3_recording_days.evidence: sustained over an interval of 46 days following LSD administration

D4_baseline.evidence: divided into three groups of equal ethanol intake based on the amount of ethanol consumed on the day before administration

D5_followup.evidence: sustained over an interval of 46 days following LSD administration

assays.assay_description: Ambulatory activity recorded as total beam breaks on x and y axes using an ATM3 infrared beam-based activity sensor over a 24-h period beginning at dark onset, on day 1 and day 8 after a single i.p. injection of 50 µg/kg LSD or saline in ethanol-naïve mice. Hourly ambulatory counts analyzed with MLM.

application_type.evidence: administration of 50 µg/kg LSD or saline

setup_habituation.evidence: habituation to the activity monitor not described

setup_restrain.evidence: ambulatory activity measured via beam interruptions; animal freely moving

food_restriction.evidence: food access during the 24 h activity recording not specified

water_restriction.evidence: water access during the 24 h activity recording not specified

time_to_assay.evidence: measured... at 1 and 8 days after the administration of 50 µg/kg LSD

sample_size.evidence: df=14 in MLM analysis suggests ~16 animals total but not explicitly stated

outcomes.summary: 50 µg/kg LSD had no significant effect on ambulatory activity compared to saline controls on either day 1 or day 8.
outcomes.evidence: The result showed no significant difference in locomotor activity comparisons between control versus the LSD-treated group utilizing a MLM for hourly ambulatory counts on day 1 (F = 0.74, df = 14, p = 0.4054) or day 8 (F < 0.01, df = 14, p = 0.9907)

B1_num_measures.evidence: ambulatory counts (interruption of total number of beams)

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: utilizing a MLM for hourly ambulatory counts

B4_ethological.evidence: locomotor beam breaks are not ethological measures

B7_automated_classification.evidence: infrared beam-based system measures position/activity only

E1_environment_type.evidence: infrared beam-based activity sensor (ATM3; Columbus Instrument)

E3_bedding.evidence: bedding not described for activity cage

E6_spatial.evidence: activity cage is a single compartment

E8_food_water.evidence: food/water provision in activity cage not described

D1_continuity.evidence: activity recorded on day 1 and day 8 after injection

D2_session_duration.evidence: over a 24 h period beginning at the dark cycle

D3_recording_days.evidence: at 1 and 8 days after the administration

D4_baseline.evidence: no pre-drug baseline activity recording described

D5_followup.evidence: activity measured at 8 days after administration

judge_notes: Two assays identified: two-bottle choice drinking and infrared beam locomotor activity. All three candidates agreed on this structure.

B2 (temporal dynamics) for the drinking assay: candidates split. Paper reports daily 24-h totals over days (between-session), not within-session time-course; scored 0 per rubric (between-session changes do not count).

D1 (continuity) for drinking: scored 1 (multiple discrete daily sessions) rather than 2 (continuous), since bottles were offered 24 h on weekdays with daily readings, not uninterrupted >=6 h monitoring of a single continuous session as a primary recording mode — though the daily session itself does cover 24 h (captured in D2/D6).
B1 for drinking: 3 distinct measures (consumption, preference, total fluid) → score 1 (2-3 bin).
E3 bedding scored 0 with low confidence — paper does not explicitly describe bedding in home cage during the drinking session.
Time_to_assay for drinking: 10 min between injection and bottle re-presentation per Methods.
